ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is a point on $AB$ such that $AD=DC$. $DE$ bisects $\angle ADC$ and intersects $AC$ at point $E$. $DF$ bisects $\angle BDC$ and intersects $BC$ at point $F$, where $\angle DFC=90^\circ$. Quadrilateral $CEDF$ is a rectangle; if $\angle B=30^\circ$ and $AD=2$, connect $BE$ and find the length of $BE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From (1), it is known that quadrilateral CEDF is a rectangle,\\
$\therefore \angle CED = \angle ECF = 90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle A = 90^\circ - \angle B = 90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$, DE$\perp$AC,\\
$\because AD = DC$,\\
$\therefore CE = AE$, $\triangle ACD$ is an equilateral triangle,\\
$\therefore \angle ACD = 60^\circ$, AC = AD = 2,\\
$\therefore AE = CE = 1$,\\
$\therefore DE = \sqrt{AD^2 - AE^2} = \sqrt{3}$,\\
$\angle DCB = \angle ECF - \angle ACD = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle DCB = \angle B$,\\
$\therefore DB = DC = AD$,\\
$\therefore DE$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\therefore BC = 2DE = 2\sqrt{3}$,\\
In $\triangle BCE$, by the Pythagorean theorem: $BE = \sqrt{CE^2 + BC^2} = \sqrt{13}$,\\
Hence, the length of BE is $\boxed{\sqrt{13}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, A, D, B are on the same bottom-side straight line, and D is between A and B; C is at the upper left, E is on side AC, and F is on side CB; in the figure CD, DE, DF are connected, and the problem statement says that quadrilateral CEDF is a rectangle, so CE is collinear with AC, CF is collinear with CB, and ∠ECF=90°, DE⊥AC. Then reason: because CEDF is a rectangle, ∠ECF=90°, and E is on AC, F is on BC, so ∠ACB=90°. Given ∠B=30°, then ∠A=90°-30°=60°. D is on AB, therefore ∠CAD=∠CAB=60°. In triangle ACD, AD=DC, so the base angle ∠CAD=∠ACD; since ∠CAD=60°, then ∠ACD=60°, thus triangle ACD is an equilateral triangle, AC=AD=DC=2. DE bisects the vertex angle ∠ADC of equilateral triangle ACD, and intersects AC at E, so E is the midpoint of AC, AE=CE=1. Therefore DE=√(AD²-AE²)=√(2²-1²)=√3. Also because ∠ACB=90°, ∠ACD=60°, so ∠DCB=90°-60°=30°. Given ∠B=30°, therefore in triangle DCB, ∠DCB=∠DBC, giving DB=DC=2. Therefore AD=DB, and D is the midpoint of AB; at the same time E is the midpoint of AC, so DE is the midline of triangle ABC, BC=2DE=2√3. Finally, in right triangle BCE, CE⊥BC, CE=1, BC=2√3, so BE=√(CE²+BC²)=√(1²+(2√3)²)=√13.
